description: DSH Measure hardening: a live check that detects stale plugin code, git-backed verification of the task ceremony, and closure of the apply_patch/shell-write/commit-add bypasses
deviation_notes: All 19 plan tasks are done and the 4 phase checkpoints are recorded. Deviations: (1) The track was reviewed by a fresh reviewer twice; Round 2 found two live defects in the new code (the metadata/deny checks ran in advise mode and under the bypass; `git add -A/-u` contributed nothing) and they were fixed before S4, plus a live-found probe error: `git cat-file -e` exits 128 for a missing object, so the S2 probe silently failed open and was switched to `git rev-parse --verify --quiet <sha>^{commit}`. (2) Tasks 1.1-1.4, 2.1-2.4 and 3.1-3.4 landed as one commit each (the plan checkboxes carry the SHAs); S3’s commit also carries the Round-2 code remediation. (3) The phase checkpoints use automated verification reports instead of user confirmation because the session runs with approvals disabled. (4) The `apply_patch`/`str_replace_editor` registry deny cannot be exercised live in this DSH build (those tools are not installed); it is covered by unit tests. (5) The shell grammar is bounded and documented as such: a heredoc body is not parsed separately, so redirect-looking text inside a document can trigger a fail-closed deny. (6) A completed task’s SHA was briefly set to a fake value to prove the live end-of-turn problem, then restored; the evidence is in measure/runs/dsh_measure_hardening_20261107/live-turn-problems.md.

sprint.goal: The DeepSeek Harness adapter proves what it claims: a live check that detects stale plugin code, git-backed verification of the task ceremony, and guards that see the write paths they previously missed.
